long_biography.plain_text:
Peter-Alexander Wacker trained in business administration and spent fourteen years in sales and planning at BMW before joining Wacker Chemie. The company had already passed through several generations of his family. He entered management, became chief executive and helped reshape its ownership before the 2006 public listing, preserving family control while opening the company to outside shareholders.

Wacker moved from the executive board to chair the supervisory board in 2008 and still holds that post. The controlling family company owns more than half of voting shares, while Blue Elephant Holding owns more than ten percent and its votes are attributed to him. These stakes establish inherited ownership alongside an executive contribution to expansion and governance. They do not make the listed group's revenue, factories, subsidiaries or balance-sheet assets his personal property.
